bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Psychologist Salary in Australia

If you are a psychologist or considering a career in psychology, knowing how your hourly rate translates into annual pay is essential for budgeting, comparing job offers, and planning your finances. This guide uses the latest award rates from the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Fair Work Commission to help you convert your hourly wage to a yearly salary, including tax and superannuation.

### How to Convert Hourly to Annual

The standard formula for converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks = annual gross pay**

For full-time employees under most awards, the ordinary hours are 38 per week. If you work part-time, use your agreed weekly hours. The result is your gross annual income before tax, Medicare levy, and super.

**Example:** A psychologist on the Health Professionals and Support Services Award at Level 1 (1st year) earns $32.44 per hour. Their annual salary is:

$32.44 × 38 × 52 = $64,109 (rounded)

If you are paid fortnightly, your gross fortnightly pay is your weekly pay multiplied by two. For the example above, weekly pay is $1,232.72, so fortnightly is $2,465.44.

### Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The national minimum wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, or $1,004.90 per week. This is the legal floor for award/agreement-free employees. However, most psychologists are covered by the Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020, which sets higher minimum rates. For instance:

- Level 1 (1st year): $32.44 per hour
- Level 1 (2nd–3rd year): $34.44 per hour
- Level 1 (4th–6th year): $37.53 per hour
- Level 1 (7th year+): $40.56 per hour

These rates increase with experience and qualifications. Always check the [pay guides](/blog) for your specific classification. If you are covered by an enterprise agreement, the rates may differ.

### Casual Loading for Psychologists

Casual employees under the award receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. This compensates for entitlements such as paid leave. For a Level 1 (1st year) psychologist, the casual rate is:

$32.44 + 25% = $40.55 per hour

When calculating annual pay for a casual, use the loaded rate and your average weekly hours. For example, 38 hours per week at $40.55 gives an annual gross of $80,614. Note that overtime rates for casuals are higher (187.5% for the first 2 hours, then 250%) because the loading is already included.

### Tax and Super on Your Annual Salary

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate your take-home pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45% on excess over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners).

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary by your employer. The maximum contribution base for 2026–27 is $270,830. For a psychologist earning $64,109, super would be approximately $7,693 per year.

Use our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) guide to understand how salary sacrifice affects your tax.

### Using Our Tools

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It then calculates your annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly pay, along with estimated tax and super. Remember that the calculator assumes a consistent 38-hour week and no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For award-specific rates, refer to the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) and [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) pages.

### Final Thoughts

Understanding your psychologist salary in Australia starts with knowing your award classification and hourly rate. Whether you are full-time, part-time, or casual, the formula remains the same: multiply by hours per week and 52 weeks. Add super on top, deduct tax and Medicare, and you have a realistic picture of your take-home pay. Always verify your rates with the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides or your enterprise agreement.
